benchmark_details.name: Business Letters
benchmark_details.overview: Models extract the send date and the sender and receiver persons from scanned German-language business letters of 1926–1935 held by the Swiss Economic Archives; a name counts when it matches a person's normalised form or one of the spellings recorded for that person.

purpose_and_intended_users.goal: Measure how well vision-language models extract correspondence metadata (send date, sender persons, receiver persons) from multi-page business letters, with each name read correctly enough to identify the person. The results are meant to guide historians, archivists and digital humanities projects in choosing a model for cataloguing letters and building correspondence networks from them.
tasks: metadata extraction from multi-page letter images
identification of sender and receiver persons
matching person names to a normalised name form
purpose_and_intended_users.limitations: The 57 letters come from a single collection on one company, are written in German between 1926 and 1935 and are mostly typewritten; results do not transfer to other archives, hands or languages. Only exact matches count (see Calculation), and the prompt does not ask for the normalised form, so a correct name spelled in a form not recorded in `ground_truths/persons.json` counts as wrong. Persons the annotators inferred from function or from the correspondence history can only be identified from the whole corpus, not from the single letter a request contains; they are excluded from the ground truth, so a model that names one is penalised. The letter title is requested but not scored; organisations and locations are not requested.
out_of_scope_uses: drawing conclusions about the persons and firms named in the letters
ranking models on languages other than German

data.source: Letters from the collection "Basler Rheinschifffahrt-Aktiengesellschaft, insbesondere über die Veräusserung des Dieselmotorbootes 'Rheinfelden' und die Gewährung eines Darlehens zur Finanzierung der Erstellung des Dieselmotorbootes 'Rhyblitz' an diese Firma" of the Swiss Economic Archives (Schweizerisches Wirtschaftsarchiv), shelf mark CH SWA HS 191 V 10, digitised on e-manuscripta: http://dx.doi.org/10.7891/e-manuscripta-54917. The collection holds 68 letters, mostly of one to three pages, on business transactions, shipping and personnel matters; 57 of them have a ground truth and form the benchmark.
data.format:
98 JPG scans of the letter pages, 2479×3508 px (3 pages in landscape orientation) and about 525 KB each. A letter is one evaluated object; its pages are named `letter<NN>_p<N>.jpg` and sent together in one request. 33 letters have one page, 15 have two, 4 three, 3 four, 1 five and 1 six. The ground truth is one JSON file per letter:

```json
{
    "transkribus_id": "1932319",
    "letter_title": ["None"],
    "send_date": ["1926-02-16"],
    "sender_persons": ["Groschupf-Jaeger, Louis", "Ritter-Dreier, Fritz"],
    "receiver_persons": ["Christ-Wackernagel, Paul"],
    "has_signatures": true
}
```

- `send_date`: the date in ISO 8601 form
- `sender_persons`, `receiver_persons`: normalised names (`Surname, Given name`); `None` when the letter names nobody
- `letter_title`: the title as written, or `None`; not scored
- `transkribus_id`: the letter's document in Transkribus; not used in scoring
- `has_signatures`: whether the letter carries handwritten signatures; used only to select letters for the test variants

`<Name>` marks a person inferred from function and date, `<<Name>>` one inferred from the correspondence history. `ground_truths/persons.json` lists 24 persons with their normalised name and the variants found in the letters (`alternateName`), plus identifiers, life dates, occupations and sources, as [Schema.org Person](https://schema.org/Person) records.
data.annotation: Anthea Alberto, Eric Decker, Pema Frick, Maximilian Hindermann, Lea Kasper, José Luis Losada Palenzuela, Sorin Marti and Elena Spadini recorded the letters and persons in the [RSF Letters Ground Truth sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1qGMVvGZV7GpU11uy0grIffDbGS2rSOj85ziFWZGyuBI/edit?usp=sharing), exported once to the JSON files in `ground_truths/`. These files are now the ground truth and are edited directly: a letter names its persons by their `name` in `persons.json`, and every spelling of a person found in the letters belongs in that person's `alternateName`, since a response name is matched against both. The persons reference list is used by the scorer only; it is not supplied to the model.
data.collection_date: Source documents: 1926–1935 (16 February 1926 to 17 August 1935). Added to the benchmark: February 2025.
data.contamination_controls: None. The scans, prompt and ground truth have been public in this repository since February 2025.

methods: zero-shot structured extraction from all pages of a letter in one request, prompt `prompts/prompt.txt`, temperature 0.0
structured JSON output requested using the `Document` dataclass (`metadata` with list-valued `send_date`, `letter_title`, `sender_persons`, `receiver_persons`)
output cap: the repository default of 16,384 tokens per request

three test variants, set in the `rules` column of `benchmarks_tests.csv`: no rules (all 57 letters); `{"skip_signatures": true, "skip_non_signatures": false}` (the 25 unsigned letters); `{"skip_signatures": false, "skip_non_signatures": true}` (the 32 signed letters)
methodology.calculation:
Three categories are scored per letter: `send_date`, `sender_persons` and `receiver_persons`. Ground truth and response are each turned into a set and compared by exact string equality.

- `send_date`: only the first date of each list is used; a `null` response date is dropped.
- persons: ground-truth persons marked as inferred (`<…>`, `<<…>>`) and `None` are removed. A response name counts as a ground-truth person if it equals the normalised name or appears in that person's `alternateName` list in `persons.json`. `null`, `None` and empty names are dropped.
- TP: in both sets
- FP: only in the response set
- FN: only in the ground-truth set

A response that parses but does not fit the letter structure scores no TP and counts every ground-truth item as FN. A response that does not parse (`answer.parsed is None`) is not scored and enters neither aggregate. TP, FP and FN are summed over all letters per category. F1 micro pools the three categories before computing F1; F1 macro averages the F1 of the three categories. Both are rounded to two decimals.
methodology.interpretation: Scores range from 0 to 1; higher is better. F1 macro, the ranking metric, gives the send date, a single item per letter, the same weight as the sender and receiver persons; F1 micro weights categories by their number of items, so persons dominate. The three test variants are scored on different letters, and their scores are not comparable with each other. A low person score can reflect a spelling not recorded in `persons.json` rather than a wrong person (see Limitations).
methodology.baseline_results: Results are on the [benchmark page](https://rise-services.rise.unibas.ch/benchmarks/p/benchmarks/business_letters) and in `results/<date>/<test_id>/` at the repository root. No fixed baseline is recorded. Compare runs only with the same prompt, rules and ground-truth revision, and report the number of scored letters with the score.
methodology.validation: The source spreadsheet records for each letter who annotated it and who checked it. Scoring is deterministic; the scorer is covered by `tests/test_business_letters_scoring.py`.
methodology.validity_justification: Set-based F1 on dates and normalised names reflects the downstream use: a catalogue record or network edge needs the correct date and the correct person, not a near spelling.

ethical_and_legal_considerations.privacy_and_anonymity: The letters name business people, mostly board members and officers of Basel shipping and trading firms, and `persons.json` adds their life dates, occupations and sources. Nothing is anonymised. Where known, the persons were born between 1857 and 1891; the latest letter dates from 1935.
ethical_and_legal_considerations.data_licensing: Source material: Public Domain Mark 1.0. Ground truth, prompts and other data created for this benchmark: CC BY 4.0.
ethical_and_legal_considerations.compliance_with_regulations: The letters are records of a private company held by the Swiss Economic Archives, which publishes the scans on e-manuscripta under the Public Domain Mark 1.0. No ethical review was carried out.
